topic: Batching, mixing, workability, transporting, placing, compaction, finishing, curing, and testing of concrete
source: 601-80.json, 681-760.json, 761-842.json, Concrete_1-50.json, Concrete_101-150.json, Concrete_151-200.json, Concrete_50-100.json, conc_201-250.json, conc_250-300.json, conc_301-350.json, conc_350-405.json

questions.q: 27. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: insufficient quantity of water makes the concrete mix harsh
insufficient quantity of water makes the concrete unworkable
excess quantity of water makes the concrete mix segregated
excess quantity of water cause bleeding in concrete
questions.explain: All these statements about the effect of water quantity (deficiency causing harshness/unworkability, excess causing segregation/bleeding) on concrete are correct.

questions.q: 35. The increase in the strength of concrete with time is
questions.explain: Concrete strength gain over time follows a non-linear curve — rapid initially and gradually slowing down, not a straight line.

questions.q: 110. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete
questions.explain: As concrete loses moisture through evaporation during drying, the cement paste loses volume, causing the concrete to shrink — this is known as drying shrinkage.

questions.q: 117. The increased cohesiveness of concrete, makes it
options: More liable for surface scaling in frosty
questions.explain: Cohesiveness refers to the ability of the fresh concrete mix to hold its ingredients together; higher cohesiveness reduces the tendency of coarser particles to separate out, i.e., reduces segregation.

questions.q: 127. At freezing point of water, concrete
questions.explain: At the freezing point, water needed for the hydration reaction turns to ice and is unavailable to react chemically with cement, so hydration (setting) effectively stops.

questions.q: 128. The datum temperature for maturity by Plowman, is
questions.explain: In Plowman's maturity concept (maturity = time × (temperature − datum temperature)), the empirically determined datum temperature below which hydration is assumed to stop is −11.7°C (11°F below freezing, i.e. 0°F).

questions.q: 129. I.S.I. has specified the full strength of concrete after
questions.explain: As per Indian Standards (I.S.I.), the characteristic/full design strength of concrete is conventionally specified and tested at 28 days of curing.

questions.q: 131. The approximate ratio of strength of cement concrete at 3 months to that of 28 days of curing
questions.explain: Concrete continues to gain strength beyond 28 days as hydration progresses further; empirically, the strength at 3 months is roughly 1.15 times the 28-day strength.

questions.q: 132. The percentage of compressive strength of concrete at 7 days to that of 28 days
questions.explain: For ordinary Portland cement concrete, the strength gained at 7 days is typically about 65% of the 28-day design strength, since a large share of hydration is still incomplete at 7 days.

questions.q: 133. The approximate ratio of direct tensile strength to direct compressive strength test of concrete
questions.explain: Concrete is inherently weak in tension compared to compression; its direct tensile strength is only about 1/10th (approximately 0.10) of its direct compressive strength.

questions.q: 135. High increase in temperature
options: Has no effect on the strength of concrete
questions.explain: A high increase in curing/ambient temperature accelerates early hydration but leads to a more porous, less uniform microstructure and rapid moisture loss, ultimately reducing the long-term strength of concrete.

questions.q: 141. Adding a thin layer of cement mortar to the surface of concrete is known as
questions.explain: Rendering (rendeting) refers to applying a thin coat/layer of cement mortar over a concrete or masonry surface, typically for finishing or protective purposes.

questions.q: 142. The breaking up and remixing of concrete that has layers to set is called
questions.explain: Resetting is the process of breaking up concrete that has already begun to set in layers and remixing it, typically done when placement is delayed beyond the initial setting time.

questions.q: 143. A concrete mix that causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth or good contact with forms, which may be due to excess of middle sized particles or a deficiency of lime materials is called
questions.explain: A harsh mix is defined precisely by this deficiency in fines/paste content or excess of medium-sized aggregate, giving it poor cohesion and a rough, difficult-to-finish surface against formwork.

questions.q: 144. A watery scum that is formed on top of concrete due to excessive water or excessive use of trowel or float is called
questions.explain: Laitance is the weak, milky layer of cement fines and water that rises to and accumulates on the surface of concrete, often from excess mixing water or over-troweling/floating.

questions.q: 147. The entrained air in concrete
questions.explain: Per the answer key, entrained air is stated to decrease resistance to weathering here — note this differs from typical air-entrainment theory (which normally improves frost/weathering resistance), but the correct option as marked in the source is (c).

questions.q: 148. The concrete mix which causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth finish, is known to possess
questions.explain: High internal friction between aggregate particles (harsh mix) resists smooth movement of material against the formwork/trowel, making it difficult to achieve a smooth surface finish.

questions.q: 151. The top diameter, bottom diameter and the height of a slump mould are
questions.explain: The standard slump mould (frustum of a cone) as per IS 7320 has a top diameter of 10 cm, bottom diameter of 20 cm, and a height of 30 cm.

questions.q: 152. In a mix if a desired slump is not obtained, the adjustment for each concrete slump is made by adjusting water content by
questions.explain: As a general rule of thumb in mix design trial adjustments, approximately 1% change in water content is made for each required change in slump to achieve the target workability.

questions.q: 154. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: the bottom and top ends of slump mould are parallel to each other
the axis of the mould is perpendicular to the end faces
the internal surface of the mould is kept clean and free from set cement
the mould is in the form of a frustum of hexagonal pyramid
questions.explain: The slump mould is in the shape of a frustum of a cone (circular cross-section), not a hexagonal pyramid, making this statement incorrect.

questions.q: 157. In slump test, each layer of concrete compacted by a steel rod 60 cm long and 16 mm diameter for
questions.explain: As per the standard slump test procedure, each of the four layers filled in the mould is tamped 25 times uniformly with a 16 mm diameter, 60 cm long tamping rod.

questions.q: 158. If the slump of concrete mix is 60 mm, its workability is
questions.explain: A slump of 25-75 mm generally corresponds to medium workability, suitable for normal reinforced concrete work placed with vibration.

questions.q: 159. The concrete having a slump of 6.5 cm, is said to be
questions.explain: A slump of around 6.5 cm falls in the plastic concrete range, indicating good flowability suitable for normal placing and compaction.

questions.q: 160. Slump test is the most widely used field test primarily because
options: it indicates the behaviour of fresh concrete under action of gravitational forces
of the simplicity of apparatus and test procedure
it measures consistency or wetness of mix
it ensures uniformity among different batches of similar concrete
questions.explain: The slump test is popular in the field mainly due to the simplicity of its apparatus (a simple cone mould and tamping rod) and the ease and speed of the test procedure.

questions.q: 161. The workability of concrete by slump test is expressed as
questions.explain: Slump is simply a linear measurement, expressed in millimetres (mm), representing the subsidence of the concrete cone.

questions.q: 162. The slump for beam slab is
questions.explain: For beams and slabs, a medium workability with a slump in the range of 50-100 mm is generally recommended for proper placement and compaction.

questions.q: 163. The workability may be defined as the amount of applied work required to compact the concrete to its maximum density. The principle is used in
questions.explain: The compaction factor test is based on the principle of determining the degree of compaction achieved by a standard amount of work done in dropping concrete through a standard height, directly relating to the definition given.

questions.q: 165. A concrete is said to be workable if
options: it can be easily mixed, placed and compacted
it has a tendency to segregate and bleed
questions.explain: Workability is defined as the ease with which concrete can be mixed, transported, placed, and compacted without segregation or bleeding.

questions.q: 167. Wp and Wf are the weights of a cylinder containing partially compacted and fully compacted concrete. If the compaction factor is 0.95, the workability of concrete is
questions.explain: A compaction factor close to 1 (such as 0.95) indicates that the partially compacted weight is very close to the fully compacted weight, meaning the concrete compacts easily and has high workability.

questions.q: 168. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: segregation is necessary for a workable concrete
consistency does not affect the workability of concrete
if the slump increases, workability decreases
if the concrete mix is dry, the slump is maximum
questions.explain: None of the first four statements is technically correct: segregation is undesirable, consistency does affect workability, higher slump means higher (not lower) workability, and a dry mix gives minimum (not maximum) slump. Hence 'none of the above' is correct.

questions.q: 172. A joint positioned so as to separate concrete from adjacent surfaces or into individual structural elements that are not in direct physical contact, is known as
questions.explain: An isolation joint is specifically provided to separate or isolate one concrete element/structure from an adjacent one so that they are not in direct physical contact and can move independently.

questions.q: 176. Minimum number of test specimens required for finding the compressive strength of concrete are
questions.explain: As per standard practice, a minimum of 3 test specimens (cubes) are cast and tested to determine the compressive strength of a concrete batch.

questions.q: 177. The preliminary test is repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimens, exceeds
questions.explain: If the range (difference) between the highest and lowest strength values of the three specimens exceeds 15 kg/cm², the test results are considered unreliable and the preliminary test must be repeated.

questions.q: 191. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
questions.explain: Shrinkage of concrete is primarily caused by the loss of water from the cement paste, so it is directly proportional to the water content present in the mix.

questions.q: 192. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
questions.explain: Since shrinkage originates in the cement paste (not the aggregates), a higher cement content in the mix directly increases the overall shrinkage of the concrete.

questions.q: 193. Shrinkage in cement concrete decrease with
questions.explain: Shrinkage is caused by moisture loss from the concrete; therefore, adding moisture (as in wet curing) counteracts and decreases the shrinkage effect.

questions.q: 194. The shrinkage of concrete is due to a change in
questions.explain: Shrinkage fundamentally refers to a reduction in the overall volume of the concrete mass as it loses moisture over time.

questions.q: 195. The concrete shrinkage is more pronounced in
questions.explain: A rich mix contains a higher proportion of cement paste (which is the shrinking component), so shrinkage is more pronounced in rich mixes compared to lean mixes.

questions.q: 196. Maximum shrinkage takes place in cement concrete after drying for
questions.explain: Drying shrinkage continues over an extended period, with the maximum shrinkage generally being observed after about one year of drying.

questions.q: 197. Poisson's ratio of concrete reduced by using
questions.explain: Using a richer mix (more cement content) tends to reduce the Poisson's ratio of the resulting concrete.

questions.q: 198. Poisson's ratio for concrete ranges between
questions.explain: The typical Poisson's ratio for concrete lies within the range of 0.11 to 0.21, depending on the mix and testing conditions.

questions.q: 199. As compared to static tests the dynamic tests on concrete give
questions.explain: Dynamic (vibration-based) testing methods generally yield a higher value of Poisson's ratio for concrete compared to static (load-based) testing methods.

questions.q: 209. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: with passage of time, the strength of cement increases
with passage of time, the strength of cement decreases
after a period of 24 months, the strength of cement reduces to 50 %
The concrete made with storage deteriorated cement, gains strength with time
questions.explain: Cement strength actually decreases (not increases) over prolonged storage time due to gradual absorption of atmospheric moisture and partial hydration, making statement (a) incorrect.

questions.q: 215. The durability of concrete is due to its resistance to
questions.explain: Durability of concrete is defined by its overall ability to resist deterioration from a combination of environmental exposure, internal disruptive forces, and chemical attack/cracking.

questions.q: 216. The inelastic behavior of concrete is due to the
options: propagation of bond and mortar cracks
presence of macro and micro cracks
questions.explain: The inelastic (non-linear stress-strain) behaviour of concrete is primarily attributed to the progressive propagation of bond cracks (at aggregate-paste interface) and mortar cracks under loading.

questions.q: 218. Which of the following does not react with concrete?
questions.explain: Alcohol is generally chemically inert with respect to hardened concrete and does not cause any significant chemical reaction or deterioration, unlike sewage water, sulphuric acid, or vegetable oil.

questions.q: 219. The presence of algae in concrete
options: causes a large entrainment of air
questions.explain: Algae contamination in concrete negatively affects it in multiple ways - reducing strength, weakening bond between paste and aggregate, and causing excessive air entrainment.

questions.q: 220. Quality control means
options: a rational use of available resources
questions.explain: Quality control fundamentally refers to the rational and efficient use of available resources (materials, labour, equipment) to consistently achieve the desired quality standards.

questions.q: 221. The cube strength of concrete exceeds the cylinder strength by (in percent)
questions.explain: Due to the difference in specimen geometry and the resulting confinement/end effects during testing, cube strength typically exceeds cylinder strength by about 20 to 25%.

questions.q: 222. For cylindrical specimens, the dimension of cylinder generally used
questions.explain: The standard cylindrical test specimen used for compressive strength testing has a diameter of 15 cm and a height of 30 cm, giving the standard height-to-diameter ratio of 2.

questions.q: 223. For cylindrical specimens, minimum strength required should be
options: 0.20 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.40 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.60 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
0.80 times the strength of 15 cm cubes
questions.explain: The compressive strength obtained from a standard cylinder is typically about 0.80 times the strength of an equivalent 15 cm cube, due to the difference in specimen shape and testing conditions.

questions.q: 224. The surface area of standard cube used for finding compressive strength of concrete is
questions.explain: The standard cube face is 15cm x 15cm = 225 cm² = 22500 mm² = 0.0225 m² - all these are equivalent expressions of the same area in different units, so all of the above is correct.

questions.q: 225. During application of load on cylindrical specimen the failure plane makes an angle of .........with the horizontal.
questions.explain: Under compressive load, cylindrical concrete specimens typically fail along a shear plane inclined at approximately 60 degrees to the horizontal (or about 30 degrees to the vertical axis of loading).

questions.q: 228. Water in excess of that required for chemical reaction in concrete results in
questions.explain: Excess water beyond what's chemically required for hydration tends to rise to the surface of freshly placed concrete, a phenomenon known as bleeding.

questions.q: 235. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
questions.explain: The allowable shear strength of concrete is generally derived as a function of, and depends upon, its compressive strength, as per design code provisions.

questions.q: 236. The strength of concrete is decreased by
questions.explain: Excessive vibration (over-vibration), impact loading, and fatigue (repeated cyclic loading) can all contribute to a decrease in the effective strength of concrete over time.

questions.q: 239. The standard size of a concrete cube for compressive strength test is
questions.explain: The standard concrete cube specimen size used for compressive strength testing is 150 mm x 150 mm x 150 mm (15 cm cube).

questions.q: 252. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to
questions.explain: Better grading of the aggregate (proper distribution of particle sizes) results in reduced voids and less water demand, which directly improves and is proportional to workability.

questions.q: 253. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to
questions.explain: As the time of transit increases, some water evaporates and initial hydration begins, causing the mix to stiffen - hence workability decreases (inversely proportional) with increasing transit time.

questions.q: 254. The shrinkage of concrete
options: is proportional to water content in the mix
questions.explain: Shrinkage of concrete is influenced by water content, cement content, and generally increases (though at a decreasing rate) with the age of concrete - all these factors together describe shrinkage behaviour.

questions.q: 260. Strength of concrete with passage of time
questions.explain: As hydration of cement continues over time, the strength of properly cured concrete continues to increase with the passage of time.

questions.q: 262. The nature of fresh concrete is
questions.explain: Freshly mixed (unset) concrete behaves as a plastic material - it can be moulded, placed, and compacted into any shape before it hardens.

questions.q: 263. Too wet concrete may cause
questions.explain: Excessively wet concrete leads to multiple defects together - reduced strength, laitance formation, segregation of ingredients, and lower final density.

questions.q: 264. The process of proper and accurate measurement of concrete ingredients for uniformity of proportion, is known
questions.explain: Batching is the specific term for the process of accurately measuring the quantities of concrete ingredients (cement, sand, aggregate, water) to ensure a uniform mix proportion.

questions.q: 265. Proper batching ensures
questions.explain: Accurate batching of concrete ingredients ensures all these desirable qualities together - economical use of materials, durability, workability, and required strength of the finished concrete.

questions.q: 267. In the batching of materials, the ingredients should be measured to a tolerance (as a percentage of batch quantity) of
questions.explain: As per standard practice, concrete batching ingredients should be measured within a tolerance of ±3% of the specified batch quantity to ensure acceptable mix accuracy.

questions.q: 268. The process of mixing some mortar in the mixer at the beginning of the first batch concrete mixing is called
questions.explain: 'Buttering' refers to the practice of first mixing a small quantity of mortar in the drum before the main batch, to coat the mixer surfaces and prevent loss of cement paste from the first actual batch.

questions.q: 270. The concrete mixers are normally classified on the basis of
options: the technique of discharging the mixed concrete
questions.explain: Concrete mixers are classified based on multiple criteria simultaneously - their discharge mechanism, batch capacity, and number of drums.

questions.q: 271. The capacity of concrete mixer is expressed in terms of
options: total volume of concrete produced per day
total volume of concrete produced in 8 hrs
total volume of concrete produced per hr
volume of concrete mix handled per batch
questions.explain: The capacity of a concrete mixer is standardly expressed as the volume of concrete mix it can handle per batch (e.g., a 150-litre mixer, 10/7 mixer, etc.).

questions.q: 277. In case of hand mixing of concrete, the extra cement to be added is
questions.explain: Since hand mixing is less efficient and thorough than machine mixing, an extra 10% cement is typically added to compensate for the reduced mixing efficiency.

questions.q: 279. Placing of concrete should preferably be done at a temperature of
questions.explain: Concrete placing is preferably carried out at a moderate temperature of around 27 ± 2°C, which is favourable for proper hydration and setting without excessive heat or cold-related issues.

questions.q: 280. To prevent segregation, the maximum vertical height for placing concrete, is
questions.explain: To prevent segregation of concrete during placing (free fall), the maximum vertical drop height allowed is limited to about 150 cm (1.5 m).

questions.q: 281. For concerting of tunnel linings, transportation of concrete is done by
questions.explain: For confined and often difficult-access locations like tunnel linings, concrete pumps are the preferred method of transportation, allowing concrete to be conveyed through pipelines to the point of placement.

questions.q: 282. Transport of concrete by pumps, is done for a distance of
questions.explain: Concrete pumps are capable of efficiently transporting concrete over relatively long distances, typically up to about 400 m, without significant loss in workability.

questions.q: 283. 'Tremie' is a
questions.explain: A 'tremie' is a water-tight pipe used to place concrete underwater or in deep foundations, preventing the concrete from mixing with water during placement.

questions.q: 285. Concrete is unsuitable for compaction by vibrator if it is
questions.explain: Very dry concrete mixes are unsuitable for vibration compaction because there isn't enough paste/fluidity for the vibrator to effectively consolidate the mix and expel air voids.

questions.q: 286. While compacting the concrete by a mechanical vibrator, the slump should not exceed
questions.explain: For effective and safe use of mechanical vibrators (avoiding segregation), the slump of the concrete being compacted should not exceed 5.0 cm.

questions.q: 287. Compaction of mechanical vibrations is suitable for
options: all the mixes except very plastic mixes
questions.explain: Mechanical vibration compaction is versatile and suitable across all grades of concrete, all structural elements, and various mix consistencies (except very plastic mixes), making it broadly applicable.

questions.q: 288. Surface vibrator is effective only when the thickness of concrete member does not exceed
questions.explain: Surface vibrators are effective only for compacting relatively thin concrete sections, with their effectiveness limited to a thickness not exceeding 200 mm.

questions.q: 289. A surface vibrator for compaction of concrete is preferred for all of the following except
questions.explain: Surface vibrators, being effective mainly for shallow/thin horizontal sections, are not preferred for columns (which are deep, vertical, heavily reinforced members) unlike footings, slabs, or pavements.

questions.q: 290. Curing
options: prevents the loss of water by evaporation
questions.explain: Curing serves multiple purposes simultaneously - it reduces shrinkage, preserves the desired properties of concrete, and prevents premature loss of moisture through evaporation.

questions.q: 291. The process by which fresh cement concrete is wetted by rain water is known as
questions.explain: Wetting of fresh concrete by rain water is not a controlled/intended process and is not technically classified as curing, wetting (in the technical sense), or raining, so 'none of the above' is correct.

questions.q: 292. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known as
questions.explain: The deliberate process of keeping concrete surfaces moist to promote continued hydration and hardening is technically known as curing.

questions.q: 293. Generally curing is allowed only after concreting of
questions.explain: Curing is generally started/allowed after an initial period of about 24 hours from concreting, once the concrete has achieved sufficient initial set to withstand water application without damage.

questions.q: 294. Steam curing is used in
questions.explain: Steam curing is primarily employed in the mass production of precast concrete elements, where accelerated strength gain is needed to allow rapid mould turnover in factory settings.

questions.q: 296. Curing of pavements, floors, roofs and slabs is done by
questions.explain: For large flat horizontal surfaces like pavements, floors, roofs, and slabs, the ponding method (creating a shallow standing pool of water on the surface) is a commonly used and effective curing technique.

questions.q: 298. Curing of concrete for long period ensures better
questions.explain: Extended/proper curing of concrete ensures improvement in all these properties together - higher strength, better wear resistance, and improved water tightness and durability.

questions.q: 299. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work is
options: 14 days for bottom of slabs of spans 4.6 m and more
21 days for bottom of beams over 6m spans
2 days for vertical sides of columns
questions.explain: These are all standard specified formwork removal periods (as per IS code guidance) for different structural elements under normal conditions using ordinary cement, so all of the above is correct.

questions.q: 301. Higher workability of concrete is required if the structure is
questions.explain: In thick, heavily reinforced sections the congestion of steel restricts free movement of concrete, so a higher workability mix is needed to ensure the concrete flows around bars and fills every corner without honeycombing.

questions.q: 304. The shuttering of a hall measuring 4 m x 5 m, can be removed after
questions.explain: For slabs/beams with spans greater than 4.5 m (props under beams/slabs spanning more than about 4.5 m), formwork should remain in place for 14 days as per standard formwork removal periods.

questions.q: 305. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: there should not be any loss of cement from the charged drum of the mixer
cement should be mixed for at least one minute
10% of water is placed in the rotating drum before adding dry material
10% of water is added after placing the other ingredients in the drum
questions.explain: All these are standard good-practice requirements for charging and mixing a concrete mixer, so the combined statement 'all of the above' is correct.

questions.q: 306. If the effective working time is 7 hours and per batch time of concrete mixer of 150 litre capacity, is
questions.explain: Multiplying the number of batches that can be produced by a 150-litre mixer within the effective 7-hour working period (based on a typical batch cycle time) gives a total output of about 18,900 litres of concrete.

questions.q: 307. The main object of compaction of concrete is
options: to provide intimate contact between the concrete and embedded materials
questions.explain: Compaction removes entrapped air, densifies the mix, and ensures concrete is in intimate contact with reinforcement/embedded parts — all these are objectives of compaction.

questions.q: 308. Non-uniform compaction may cause the concrete
questions.explain: Uneven compaction leaves pockets of poorly consolidated concrete, making it porous, non-homogeneous, and weaker in strength — hence all effects occur together.

questions.q: 309. The compaction of concrete, improves
questions.explain: Proper compaction expels air voids, which simultaneously increases density, strength, and durability of the hardened concrete.

questions.q: 310. The final operation of finishing floors, is known
questions.explain: Trowelling is carried out last, after floating, to produce a smooth, dense, and hard surface finish on concrete floors.

questions.q: 311. The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface, is known as
questions.explain: Screeding is the process of striking off excess concrete with a straightedge to remove humps and hollows and bring the surface to the required level.

questions.q: 312. The ratio of the length and breadth of wooden float, is
questions.explain: A wooden float used for finishing concrete surfaces typically has a length-to-breadth ratio of about 7.5, giving a long narrow tool for smoothing the surface.

questions.q: 313. Construction joints are provided
options: where BM and SF are small
where it is supported by another member
at 18 m apart in huge structures
in concrete wall at sill level of windows
questions.explain: Construction joints are located at points of low bending moment/shear, at supports, at regular intervals in large structures, and at window sill levels in walls — all of these are valid locations.

questions.q: 314. The surface where two successive placements of concrete meet, is known as
questions.explain: A construction joint is, by definition, the interface formed where one concreting operation stops and the next placement begins.

questions.q: 315. A construction joint is provided where
options: it is supported by other member
questions.explain: Construction joints are best located where internal forces (BM and SF) are minimal or where the member is supported, so all the listed conditions are appropriate locations.

questions.q: 316. Horizontal construction joins in concrete walls are generally provided at
questions.explain: Horizontal construction joints in walls are conventionally placed at soffit level, window sill level, and floor level, since these are natural break points in the pour.

questions.q: 317. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: construction joints in columns are provided a few cm below the junction of beam
construction joints in columns are provided at the bottom haunching
construction joints in beam and slabs are provided within middle third
construction joints are generally provided in positions subjected to least shear force
questions.explain: Each statement correctly describes accepted practice for locating construction joints in columns, beams and slabs, so the combined answer 'all of the above' applies.

questions.q: 318. Joints in concrete structures, are provided
options: to reduce the tensile stresses likely to be developed due to evaporation of water
to minimize the change in the dimensions of the slab
questions.explain: Joints in concrete relieve tensile stresses from shrinkage/temperature effects, limit dimensional change, and control cracking, so all listed purposes are correct.

questions.q: 319. Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structures exceeds
questions.explain: Expansion joints are generally introduced in long concrete structures once their length exceeds about 40 m, to accommodate thermal movement.

questions.q: 320. According to the recommendations of IS:456-2000, expansion joints
options: are provided where plane changes abruptly
are provided to ensure minimum resistance
do not carry reinforcement across them
questions.explain: IS:456-2000 recommends expansion joints at abrupt plan changes, designed to offer minimum resistance to movement, supported independently, and without reinforcement crossing them — all points are valid.

questions.q: 321. Construction joints are generally provided in concrete
questions.explain: Construction joints are a common feature in roads, retaining walls, channel linings, and tunnel linings wherever concreting must be carried out in separate stages.

questions.q: 322. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: construction joins are necessarily planned for their locations
expansion joints are provided to accommodate thermal expansion
construction joints are provided to control shrinkage cracks
expansion joints need not be provided in foundation concrete
questions.explain: Each statement is a correct principle about joint design and location, so together they form the correct combined answer.

questions.q: 327. The risk of segregation is more for
questions.explain: Wetter mixes, a larger proportion of maximum-size aggregate, and coarser grading all reduce cohesion of the mix, increasing the likelihood that coarse aggregate separates from the mortar (segregation).

questions.q: 328. The process by which fresh cement concrete is compacted to remove the air bubbles is known as
questions.explain: Compaction is the specific operation of expelling entrapped air from freshly placed concrete, typically by vibration or ramming.

questions.q: 329. Maturity of concrete means
options: sum of product of temperature & time
questions.explain: Maturity is a concept that combines the effects of curing temperature and time (the temperature-time factor), used to estimate strength gain, rather than simply age.

questions.q: 355. An increase in strain in a concrete member at constant stress is called
questions.explain: Creep is defined as the gradual increase in strain in concrete under a sustained constant stress over time.

questions.q: 356. Strain in concrete at zero stress is called
questions.explain: Shrinkage is the volumetric/strain change that occurs in concrete due to moisture loss even in the absence of any applied stress.

questions.q: 367. What is the process of smoothening the surface of newly placed concrete with a trowel called?
questions.explain: The operation of smoothening and levelling the surface of freshly placed concrete is termed floating, carried out with a float/trowel before final finishing.

questions.q: 372. Steel mould used for slump test is in the form of :
questions.explain: The standard slump test mould is a frustum of a cone (Abrams cone), which is filled with concrete and lifted vertically to measure the resulting slump.

questions.q: 375. The concrete in which preliminary tests are preformed for designing the mix is called:
questions.explain: Controlled concrete refers to concrete whose mix proportions are determined and controlled through preliminary laboratory tests to meet specified strength and durability requirements.

questions.q: 376. Concreting should be stopped when temperature falls below …
questions.explain: Concreting operations are generally stopped once the ambient temperature drops below about 4.5°C, since hydration slows drastically and frost damage risk increases.

questions.q: 380. Modulus of rupture of concrete is measure of :
questions.explain: Modulus of rupture is obtained from a beam flexure test and represents the flexural (bending) tensile strength of concrete.

questions.q: 382. The durability of concrete is proportion to :
questions.explain: Durability of concrete is closely linked to the cement-aggregate ratio, since it governs the density and impermeability of the paste matrix surrounding the aggregate.

questions.q: 383. Plain cement concrete is strong in taking :
questions.explain: Plain (unreinforced) concrete has high compressive strength but is comparatively weak in tension and shear, hence it is primarily used to resist compressive stress.

questions.q: 384. The removal of excess air after placing concrete helps in increasing the strength of concrete by :
questions.explain: Proper compaction that removes entrapped/excess air from freshly placed concrete has been found to increase its strength by roughly 15 to 20%.

questions.q: 386. The cold bent test is conducted in a steel bar to determine :
questions.explain: The cold bend test checks the ductility of reinforcement bars by bending a test specimen through a specified angle, typically 90 degrees, without cracking.

questions.q: 389. To determine the modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is
questions.explain: The standard flexural (modulus of rupture) test specimen for concrete is a beam of size 150 x 150 x 700 mm as per Indian Standard specifications.

questions.q: 390. The steel mould used for slump test is in the form of :
questions.explain: As with the standard slump test mould, it is shaped as a frustum of a cone (Abrams cone) open at both ends.

questions.q: 395. The individual variation between test strength of sample should not be more than
questions.explain: As per test acceptance criteria, the deviation of an individual test result from the average of the sample should not exceed ±15% of the average value.

questions.q: 400. Age factor for permissible compressive stress in concrete after six months is :
questions.explain: Concrete continues to gain strength with age, so codes allow an age factor of 1.20 to be applied to the permissible compressive stress for concrete that is six months old.

questions.q: 2. The workability of concrete is defined as the
options: ease with which it can be mixed, transported and placed in position in a homogeneous state
breaking up of cohesion in a mass of concrete
separation of water or water-cement mixture from the freshly mixed concrete
questions.explain: Workability describes how easily fresh concrete can be mixed, transported, placed, and compacted without segregation, while remaining homogeneous.

questions.q: 3. Segregation in concrete results in
questions.explain: Segregation separates coarse aggregate, mortar, and water unevenly, which can cause honeycombing, porous layers, and surface scaling all at once depending on where separation occurs.

questions.q: 4. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
questions.explain: An excess of coarser particles relative to fines reduces the paste's ability to lubricate the mix, making the concrete harsh and difficult to work.

questions.q: 6. Reinforced cement concrete is equally strong in taking
questions.explain: By combining concrete (strong in compression) with steel reinforcement (strong in tension) and proper detailing for shear, RCC is designed to resist tensile, compressive, and shear stresses effectively.

questions.q: 11. The characteristic, which makes the concrete a versatile and widely used material of modern construction, is the possibility of
options: controlling the properties of concrete by using appropriate ingredients
molding the concrete in any desired shape
complete mechanization of concrete preparation and its placing process
questions.explain: Concrete's versatility comes from a combination of factors: controllable properties through mix design, moldability into any shape, and full mechanization of production and placement, all of which together make it widely used.

questions.q: 14. Minimum number of days required for curing fresh laid concrete under normal atmospheric condition is
questions.explain: Under normal atmospheric conditions, a minimum curing period of 7 days is generally specified to allow adequate hydration and strength gain of concrete.

questions.q: 41. Maturity of concrete means
options: sum of product of temperature and time
questions.explain: Maturity of concrete is a concept defined as the sum of the products of curing temperature and time, used to estimate strength development.

questions.q: 60. The slump test of concrete is used to measure its
questions.explain: The slump test primarily measures the consistency (a measure of wetness/workability) of fresh concrete by observing how much it settles after removing the slump cone.

questions.q: 61. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
questions.explain: A preliminary test is conducted in the laboratory on trial mixes before actual construction to determine and verify the proportions needed to achieve the required strength.

questions.q: 64. The concrete in which no preliminary tests are performed for designing the mix is called
questions.explain: Ordinary (nominal mix) concrete is proportioned using fixed ratios (e.g., 1:2:4) without conducting preliminary trial mix tests, unlike controlled/design mix concrete.

questions.q: 69. The importance of batching is to obtain
questions.explain: Accurate batching of ingredients ensures the desired mix proportions, which in turn affects and helps achieve strength, workability, and durability all together.

questions.q: 70. The mixer, which produces a steady stream of concrete as long as it is in operation, is known as
questions.explain: A continuous mixer feeds materials in continuously and discharges a steady, uninterrupted stream of mixed concrete for as long as it operates, unlike batch mixers which discharge in batches.

questions.q: 71. For continuous transportation of concrete, the method used is
options: transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by belt concrete conveyors
questions.explain: Belt conveyors provide a continuous, uninterrupted method of transporting concrete over distances, unlike wheel barrows or pumps used for other applications.

questions.q: 72. In transportation of concrete by pumps
options: the slump should not be less than 50 mm and more than 80mm
the water cement ratio should remain between 0.5 to 0.65
the number of bends in a pipe line should be as small as possible
questions.explain: Successful pumping of concrete requires appropriate slump range, controlled water-cement ratio, and minimizing pipeline bends to reduce friction losses, so all conditions apply together.

questions.q: 73. When the concrete mix is too wet, it caused
questions.explain: A too-wet concrete mix leads to segregation of aggregates, reduces density after settlement, and produces excess laitance (weak cement-water layer) at the surface, all occurring together.

questions.q: 74. The object of compaction is to
options: ensure intimate contact between the concrete and the surface of reinforcement
questions.explain: Compaction serves multiple purposes simultaneously: removing entrapped air, achieving maximum density, and ensuring the concrete surrounds reinforcement completely.

questions.q: 75. For compacting large sections of mass concrete in structures, the types of vibrator used is
questions.explain: Internal (needle) vibrators are inserted directly into the concrete mass and are best suited for compacting large sections of mass concrete.

questions.q: 76. For compacting plain concrete or one-way reinforced concrete floors, the vibrator used is
questions.explain: Screed vibrators are mounted on a screed board and are ideal for compacting relatively thin, flat sections like plain concrete or one-way reinforced floors.

questions.q: 77. After the curing of 28 days, the concrete gains strength upto (As per IS)
questions.explain: By IS convention, 28-day cured concrete is considered to have gained 100% of its designated characteristic (design) strength, though it continues to gain further strength beyond 28 days.

questions.q: 78. In concrete walls, construction joints should be provided at the
questions.explain: Construction joints in walls are conveniently located at floor levels, lintel soffit levels, and window sill levels, as these are natural break points in the wall's structural continuity.

questions.q: 79. The construction joints in cement concrete
options: should be located where bending moment is large
should be located where shear force is large
should not be provided at the corners
should be spaced at a distance of 3 m part in case of huge structures
questions.explain: Construction joints should be avoided at corners since these are critical stress concentration zones and joints there could weaken structural integrity.

questions.q: 80. The construction joints are generally provided in concrete
questions.explain: Construction joints are a common feature across many types of concrete structures including roads, retaining walls, and tunnel linings, wherever concreting must be done in stages.

questions.q: 83. Strain in concrete at zero stress is called
questions.explain: Shrinkage is the strain that develops in concrete over time due to moisture loss, occurring even without any externally applied load (zero stress).

questions.q: 85. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to
questions.explain: Well-graded aggregate reduces voids and internal friction, allowing the mix to flow more easily, so workability increases with better grading.

questions.q: 88. The approx. ratio of the strength of the cement conc. of 7 days to that of 28 days is
questions.explain: Concrete typically develops about 65% of its 28-day strength by 7 days of curing, giving an approximate ratio of 0.65.

questions.q: 89. The approx. ratio of the direct tensile strength to direct compressible strength test is
questions.explain: The direct tensile strength of concrete is generally only about 1/10th (0.10) of its direct compressive strength, reflecting concrete's inherent weakness in tension.

questions.q: 90. The approx. ratio of direct tensile strength to flexural strength is
questions.explain: The direct tensile strength of concrete is approximately half (0.5) of its flexural strength (modulus of rupture), since flexural tests measure extreme fiber stress differently from direct tension.

questions.q: 91. A concrete having a slump of 6.5, is said to be
questions.explain: A slump value of around 6.5cm falls within the range classified as plastic concrete, indicating moderate workability.

questions.q: 92. Concrete is unsuitable for compaction by a vibrator if it is
questions.explain: Plastic (wet, high-slump) concrete does not need mechanical vibration and is actually unsuitable for it, since vibration can cause segregation and bleeding in already-flowable mixes.

questions.q: 93. The increased cohesiveness of concrete, makes it
options: more liable for surface scaling in frosty weather.
questions.explain: Greater cohesiveness means the constituent materials hold together better, reducing the tendency of the mix to segregate during handling and placement.

questions.q: 94. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete on drying
questions.explain: As moisture evaporates from ordinary cement concrete after casting, the paste loses volume and the concrete undergoes drying shrinkage.

questions.q: 114. High temperature
options: has no effect on the strength of concrete
questions.explain: Elevated curing or ambient temperatures generally lead to reduced ultimate strength of concrete due to faster but less uniform hydration and increased porosity.

questions.q: 115. Placing of concrete should preferably be done at a temperature of
questions.explain: Placing of concrete is preferably done at a moderate temperature of about 27°C ± 2°C, matching standard test/curing temperature conditions for optimal hydration.

questions.q: 116. Higher workability of concrete is required if the structure is
questions.explain: Thick, heavily reinforced sections have congested reinforcement and limited space, requiring higher workability so the concrete can flow around bars and fully compact.

questions.q: 118. Segregation is responsible for
questions.explain: Segregation of concrete ingredients can lead to a combination of defects including honeycombing, porous layers, and surface scaling, depending on where the separation occurs.

questions.q: 119. The concrete mix which causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth finish, possess
questions.explain: A harsh concrete mix, lacking sufficient fines/paste to lubricate the aggregates, makes it difficult to achieve a smooth surface finish.

questions.q: 120. The top diameter, bottom diameter and the height of a slump mould are:
questions.explain: The standard slump cone has a top diameter of 10cm, bottom diameter of 20cm, and a height of 30cm, as specified by IS code.

questions.q: 121. If the slump of a concrete mix is 60 mm, its workability is
questions.explain: A slump value of 60mm falls within the medium workability range as per standard slump classification tables.

questions.q: 123. In slump test, each layer of concrete is compacted by a steel rod 60 cm long and of 16 mm diameter for
questions.explain: As per the standard slump test procedure, each of the four layers of concrete filled in the mould is tamped 25 times with the standard tamping rod.

questions.q: 127. The preliminary test is repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimens, exceeds
questions.explain: If the compressive strength results of three specimens from a preliminary test vary by more than 15 kg/cm², the test is considered unreliable and must be repeated.

questions.q: 133. Proper batching ensures
questions.explain: Accurate batching of ingredients in the correct proportions ensures the concrete achieves economy, workability, and the intended strength simultaneously.

questions.q: 135. The process of mixing, transporting, placing and compacting concrete using ordinary port land cement should not take more than
questions.explain: To prevent premature stiffening and loss of workability, the entire process from mixing to compacting concrete with ordinary Portland cement should be completed within 30 minutes.

questions.q: 136. For concreting tunnel linings, transportation of concrete is done by
questions.explain: Pumping is the preferred method for transporting concrete in confined and elongated spaces like tunnel linings, where other methods are impractical.

questions.q: 137. Transport of concrete by pumps, is done for a distance of
questions.explain: Concrete pumps are capable of effectively transporting concrete over distances of up to about 400m through pipelines.

questions.q: 138. To prevent segregation, the maximum height for placing concrete, is
questions.explain: To avoid segregation caused by the impact of falling concrete, the maximum free-fall height for placing concrete should be limited to about 100cm (1m).

questions.q: 139. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known
questions.explain: Curing is the deliberate process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature in concrete after placement to allow proper hydration and hardening.

questions.q: 140. Curing of pavements, floors, roofs and slabs, is done by
questions.explain: For flat horizontal surfaces like pavements, floors, roofs, and slabs, ponding (creating a shallow water layer over the surface) is the commonly used curing method.

questions.q: 141. Curing a concrete for long period ensures better
questions.explain: Extended curing periods allow more complete hydration, which improves volume stability, strength, water-tightness, and overall durability of concrete all together.

questions.q: 142. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work, is:
options: 15 days for bottom slabs 4.6 m and more
2 days for vertical sides of columns
questions.explain: Standard formwork removal periods for ordinary cement concrete vary by member: about 2 days for columns, 7 days for beam soffits, and 15 days for larger slabs, so all these apply.

questions.q: 143. While compacting the concrete by a mechanical vibrator, the slump should not exceed
questions.explain: When mechanical vibration is used for compaction, the concrete mix should be relatively stiff, with slump not exceeding about 5.0cm to avoid segregation.

questions.q: 144. The shuttering of a hall measuring 4m × 5m, can be removed after
questions.explain: For a slab of moderate span (like 4m × 5m), soffit shuttering can generally be removed after 7 days under normal curing conditions.

questions.q: 145. Too wet concrete may cause
questions.explain: An overly wet concrete mix can simultaneously cause reduced strength, excessive laitance formation at the surface, and segregation of the ingredients.

questions.q: 146. Non-uniform compaction may cause the concrete
questions.explain: Uneven compaction leaves some parts under-compacted, resulting in porosity, a non-homogeneous structure, and consequently reduced strength throughout the member.

questions.q: 147. The compaction of concrete, improves
questions.explain: Proper compaction removes air voids, increasing density, which in turn improves both the strength and durability of the hardened concrete.

questions.q: 148. For compacting plain concrete road surface of thickness less than 20 cm, we use
questions.explain: Screed vibrators, mounted on a beam that runs across the surface, are well suited for compacting thin plain concrete road slabs less than 20cm thick.

questions.q: 149. The final operation of finishing floors, is known as
questions.explain: Trowelling is the final finishing operation performed on a concrete floor surface to achieve a smooth, dense, and polished finish.

questions.q: 150. The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface, is known as
questions.explain: Floating is the operation performed after screeding to remove minor surface humps and hollows, leaving a relatively level, uniform surface before trowelling.

questions.q: 151. The surface where two successive placements of concrete meet, is known as
questions.explain: A construction joint is formed at the interface where one concrete pour ends and the next placement begins, joining two successive batches of concrete.

questions.q: 152. Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structures exceeds
questions.explain: Expansion joints are typically provided in long concrete structures once the length exceeds about 45m, to accommodate thermal expansion and contraction movements.

questions.q: 161. The entrained air in concrete
questions.explain: Entrained air bubbles act like tiny ball bearings within the mix, improving the flow and workability of fresh concrete.

questions.q: 171. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
questions.explain: The allowable (permissible) shear strength value used in design is directly based on the concrete's own inherent shear strength characteristics.

questions.q: 173. The shrinkage of concrete
options: is proportional to water content is the mix
questions.explain: Shrinkage in concrete is influenced together by the water content, cement content, and it accumulates further as the concrete ages, so all these factors are relevant.

questions.q: 180. Strength of concrete with passage of time
questions.explain: As hydration of cement continues over time, concrete progressively gains strength, so its strength increases with the passage of time.

questions.q: 182. The process of proper and accurate measurement of concrete ingredients for uniformity of proportion, is known
questions.explain: Batching is the process of accurately measuring the quantities of cement, aggregates, and water to maintain consistent mix proportions.

questions.q: 186. Endurance limit of mild steel is approximately equal to
questions.explain: The endurance (fatigue) limit of mild steel is approximately 0.5 times its ultimate tensile strength, a commonly cited approximation in material science.

questions.q: 188. The bond strength between steel and concrete is due to
questions.explain: The bond between reinforcing steel and surrounding concrete develops through a combination of both frictional resistance and adhesive chemical bonding at the interface.

questions.q: 195. Which type of vibrator is generally used in concrete work?
questions.explain: The needle (internal) vibrator is the most commonly used type in general concrete work, as it can be inserted directly into the concrete mass for thorough compaction.

questions.q: 197. In order to have segregation in concrete, its dropping height should be less than
questions.explain: To avoid segregation during placement, the free-fall (dropping) height of concrete should be kept below approximately 100cm.

questions.q: 199. For finding compressive strength of concrete, the minimum number of cubes required is
questions.explain: As per standard testing practice, a minimum of 3 concrete cubes are cast and tested to determine the average compressive strength for a given sample.

questions.q: 202. Low water concrete result in
questions.explain: Insufficient water in a concrete mix produces a stiff, dry mixture that becomes very difficult to work with, resulting in non-workability.

questions.q: 204. The behavior of concrete under instantaneous loads is
questions.explain: Under instantaneous (short-duration) loading, concrete behaves approximately as an elastic material, following a near-linear stress-strain relationship.

questions.q: 206. The concrete may achieve 100% strength after
questions.explain: While 28-day strength is used as the standard design reference, concrete continues to gain strength gradually and may reach close to its full/ultimate strength after about 1 year of curing.

questions.q: 211. For compacting large sections of mass concrete in structures, the type of vibrator used is:
questions.explain: Internal (needle) vibrators are best suited for compacting large volumes of mass concrete by inserting them directly into the concrete.

questions.q: 216. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
questions.explain: An excess of middle-sized particles relative to finer material can lead to poor paste distribution and a harsh, difficult-to-work concrete mix.

questions.q: 217. Concrete can take tension up to
options: 10% of the compressive strength of steel
10% of the combined compressive strength of concrete & R/F
10% of the total tensile strength of the section
questions.explain: Concrete's tensile strength is generally only about 10% of its own compressive strength, reflecting its characteristic weakness in tension relative to compression.

questions.q: 220. After 28 days concrete acquires
questions.explain: While 28-day strength is the standard reference for design, concrete at this stage has actually already gained more than 80% of its long-term ultimate strength.

questions.q: 223. Cube test is used to determine
questions.explain: The standard cube test is specifically designed to determine the compressive strength of concrete, the most commonly required strength parameter.

questions.q: 225. The process of keeping concrete moist for a certain period after its finishing, is known as
questions.explain: Curing is defined as the process of maintaining adequate moisture in concrete for a specified period after finishing, to ensure proper hydration and strength gain.

questions.q: 226. Compaction test for concrete is done to determine
questions.explain: The compaction factor test is specifically designed to assess the workability of concrete mixes, particularly those with low water content where the slump test is less reliable.

questions.q: 231. The ultimate load of a balanced reinforced concrete beam is proportional to
options: crushing strength of concrete and/or tensile strength of the steel
questions.explain: In a balanced section, both the concrete's crushing (compressive) strength and the steel's tensile strength reach their limiting values simultaneously, so the ultimate load depends on both.

questions.q: 235. The test conducted in the labouratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
questions.explain: A preliminary test is carried out in the laboratory on specimens made from trial concrete mixes to establish suitable proportions before actual construction begins.
